about: Switch model number -> SoC / board codename -> where its drivers come from and how the GitHub Actions workflow produces them. 'build' says HOW: ci = compiled and test-signed on a Windows runner (tools/ci/Build-AllDrivers.ps1 -Model <id>); upstream-binaries = taken from a published upstream release and checked against SHA-256 values in this repository; none = nothing to build. 'status' says whether this repository can produce a driver set for the model. Nothing here claims a driver works on hardware.

HAC-001.name: Nintendo Switch (original, Erista / Tegra X1)
HAC-001.note: Built and test-signed by .github/workflows/build-all-drivers.yml (Windows runner with WDK); tools/build/assemble_build.py puts the result in build/HAC-001/drivers/. TegraGpu is built by build-erista-gpu.yml (called from the same run); its probe driver needs NVIDIA firmware, which the run imports with fwfetch from a private bundle you supply. Not built in the authoring environment, no real-console test of the whole set. SwitchCenter / SwitchPatcher come from the apps job; tools/ci/verify_build.py checks every .sys (ARM64, native, signed, INF/CAT present).

HAC-001-01.name: Nintendo Switch (2019 revision, Mariko / Tegra X1+)
HAC-001-01.note: This repository has no driver set for Iowa (docs/DRIVER-INVENTORY.md: 'Iowa は専用の枠なし'). The Erista and Lite sets are NOT reused: board, power and I2C wiring are not shown to match. The workflow lists this model as skipped.

HDH-001.name: Nintendo Switch Lite (Mariko / Tegra X1+)
HDH-001.note: Built and test-signed by the same workflow with tools/ci/drivers-t214-hoag.json, written from drivers/t214-hoag/docs/hdh001/build-drivers.sh and the per-driver READMEs. The TegraGpu probe (and its SwitchFan bridge) is built by build-lite-gpu.yml, called from the same run; it needs NVIDIA firmware imported with fwfetch (profile lite), otherwise only TegraGpuCore.lib is built. SwitchCenter / SwitchPatcher are published for win-arm64 by the apps job. Every .sys is checked by tools/ci/verify_build.py (ARM64, native, signed, INF/CAT present). Not built in the authoring environment, no real-console test. Not in the set: the WINARM SD-miniport variant (needs a card-specific private header made with the target generator) and a display/Vulkan GPU driver (the GPU package is a bring-up probe, not a display driver).

HEG-001.name: Nintendo Switch OLED (Mariko / Tegra X1+)
HEG-001.note: Built and test-signed from source by .github/workflows/build-all-drivers.yml (Windows runner, WDK + clang-cl), the same way as HAC-001 / HDH-001, with tools/ci/drivers-t214-aula.json: swhid.sys + swbatt.sys (windows-switch sources in drivers/t214-aula/drivers, WDM, no INF: w64.cmd installs them by registry), swagentsvc.exe (clang-cl, ARM64), and switchbt / switchaudio / switchwifi from the shared winx-family sources in drivers/t214-hoag (same HWIDs and versions as the INFs in drivers/t214-aula/kit; the INFs, wifi_sign.ps1, w64.cmd and the other scripts are copied unchanged from kit/ so build/HEG-001/drivers/agent/ has the windows-switch layout). Not built in the authoring environment; no real-console test; the binaries are NOT byte-identical to windows-switch v0.8.0 (the only OLED-reported set). The earlier 'download the upstream release and check SHA-256' path is still available: run the workflow with heg001_upstream = true.
